about: The posts the town hires or appoints somebody into, and what each department says it employs.

conclusions.basis: The per-school staff rosters in the annual report, against the Fire and Police rosters and the DPW establishment.
conclusions.claim: The schools employ more people than the rest of the town put together, six times over
conclusions.detail: Before any question about who is growing: this is the scale of the town’s workforce, and one part of it is nearly all of it. The schools name 250 members of staff in FY2025. Every other part of the town that publishes a count — the Fire Department, the Police Department and the Department of Public Works — comes to 79 between them.

others.unit: in every other department that publishes a count

conclusions.not_shown: The departments that publish nothing. Their staff are in no count here and their absence is not a small number.
conclusions.so_what: A conversation about town staffing is mostly a conversation about the schools.

conclusions.basis: Each department’s own published count, first published year against last, with any year reading under half its predecessor dropped as a short read rather than a cut.
conclusions.claim: One department has fewer people than it did. The rest are flat or larger
conclusions.detail: Who added staff and who lost it, over the years each one publishes. The Fire Department is down 5, from 45 to 40, all of it in the on-call roll while its career staff doubled. The schools are up 34 since FY2011, the Police Department up 3, and the Department of Public Works unchanged at 14 posts.
conclusions.not_shown: Hours or FTE. A call firefighter and a classroom teacher are one person each here.
conclusions.so_what: Only one part of the town has visibly shed people, and not the part usually named.

employers.kind: career staff plus the low end of the on-call range
posts in the establishment it states

grain: POSTS AND NAMED STAFF, never a payroll. One row is one appointed post, or one person named on a department roster. No salary is read or inferred.
not_established: What anybody is paid. No salary is read here, and none is inferred from a post’s name.

How many people the town employs. A DPW labourer, a library assistant and a town hall clerk hold no appointed post and appear in no roster — the wage list that would give a headcount stopped naming departments after FY2016.
FTE. A career post and an on-call post are not the same job and cannot be netted against each other.

A town total. The departments that describe their staffing do it in whichever form that year’s department head chose — a count, a range, an establishment post by post, a list of names — and those are different quantities.

sources.note: Read by scripts/extract_personnel.py. A post that states no membership and no term is an officer rather than a board seat — the town’s own distinction, not ours.
